children: Brazilian aerospace manufacturer Embraer will partner with Mahindra Group for the Indian Air Force’s Multi-Role Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme, under which the IAF is seeking 60 transport aircraft. Embraer is offering its KC-390 Millennium for the programme.

The procurement is aimed at beginning the replacement of the IAF’s ageing transport fleet and includes an option to add another 50 per cent to the initial requirement. The twin-engine KC-390 is already in service with Brazil, Portugal and other air forces.

Mahindra will remain Embraer’s partner for the military transport aircraft programme. For its civilian aircraft business in India, Embraer is separately working with the Adani Group to address demand for regional connectivity and commercial aviation.
Embraer had demonstrated the C-390 in India in 2023 and subsequently evaluated potential partners for the MTA programme before selecting Mahindra.

The company is preparing its response to the IAF programme within the procurement timeline. The KC-390 is being positioned for the IAF’s medium transport requirements, including as a replacement for older aircraft such as the AN-32.
Five Indian companies — Mahindra, Tata, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Reliance Defence and Adani — have received the Request for Proposal from the Defence Ministry for the IAF programme.

The KC-390 is competing with other aircraft, including the C-130J being offered by the Tata-Lockheed Martin team. Embraer has reported global fleet availability of 93 per cent and mission accomplishment of 99 per cent for the KC-390, with one operator with more than four aircraft recording 100 per cent availability during the previous month.
The aircraft has also undergone operations from unpaved desert runways during a week-long trial with the UAE Air Force.
Embraer has a global order book of around 70 KC-390 aircraft, including an order for 10 aircraft from the UAE and two additional aircraft from Colombia.
The company is also looking at India as a potential base for expanding its global aircraft supply chain and maintenance, repair and overhaul network as its KC-390 fleet grows internationally.
